# What Sourcegraph access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a value is forty hexadecimal characters, so the run twice over
# and eight more is one, and the instance identifier a licensed instance writes
# is the run once. With the prefix in front that makes a token forty-four
# characters, fifty where it carries the word a development instance writes and
# sixty-one where it carries a hexadecimal identifier. Where a case turns on the
# alphabet, it carries the same run spelled uppercase or carried on past f
# instead.

patterns: sourcegraph-access-token

# The three forms Sourcegraph's own secret formats page gives an expression for,
# in the places a token is written. They are one credential to a caller: the
# instance identifier says which instance issued a token rather than what the
# token may do, and the vendor's own parser strips whichever prefix and
# identifier it is handed and looks the same forty characters up.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token carrying the identifier a licensed instance writes
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token carrying the identifier a development instance writes
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_local_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token in the header the graphql api reads it from
in:       Authorization: token sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      Authorization: token «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token in the configuration file the cli reads
in:       {"endpoint":"https://sourcegraph.example.com","accessToken":"sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567"}
out:      {"endpoint":"https://sourcegraph.example.com","accessToken":"«sourcegraph-access-token»"}

case:     a token on a curl command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: token sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567" https://sourcegraph.example.com/.api/graphql
out:      curl -H "Authorization: token «sourcegraph-access-token»" https://sourcegraph.example.com/.api/graphql

case:     a token on a command line the cli reads its environment from
in:       SRC_ENDPOINT=https://sourcegraph.example.com SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_local_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 src search foo
out:      SRC_ENDPOINT=https://sourcegraph.example.com SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=«sourcegraph-access-token» src search foo

# The alphabet an identifier and a value are written in: hexadecimal in either
# case. Sourcegraph writes the expression on its secret formats page and the
# parser its API authenticates with both as [a-fA-F0-9], so an uppercased token
# is one the vendor accepts, and the generator writes lowercase — which makes an
# uppercase value a string nothing mints and everything authenticates. A
# character outside the alphabet is no part of either.

case:     an uppercase value
in:       sgp_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     one uppercase character in a value
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456F
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     an uppercase identifier
in:       sgp_0123456789ABCDEF_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a value carrying letters past f
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123
out:      sgp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123

case:     a value carrying a hyphen
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef01234567

# The lengths either side of forty. The count is the vendor's own and is read as
# a count rather than a floor: thirty-nine characters are not a value, and
# forty-one are a value and one character that belongs to no credential. The
# second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the match — a
# boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real token
# written against a digit would come through whole.

case:     a value of forty characters is a token
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a value of thirty-nine characters is not
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456
out:      sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»8

# Which of the three forms a candidate is read as, which is settled by what
# stands behind the prefix and never by trying one reading after another. The
# word opens with a letter no hexadecimal identifier and no value is written
# with; the character sixteen along divides the other two, being the separator
# where a token carries an identifier and a seventeenth character of the value
# where it does not. An identifier of seventeen characters is neither, and a
# value with a separator behind it is the form carrying no identifier.

case:     a separator seventeen characters along is neither reading
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_0123456789abcdef0_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an identifier a character short
in:       sgp_0123456789abcde_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_0123456789abcde_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a value with a separator behind it is the form carrying no identifier
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the word of the local identifier written uppercase
in:       sgp_LOCAL_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_LOCAL_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the word of the local identifier with no separator behind it
in:       sgp_local0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_local0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# An identifier Sourcegraph never writes. It states that the identifier is not
# verified when a token is used, so a token whose identifier was edited still
# authenticates — and what is read here is the grammar the vendor gives its own
# scanners, which names two identifiers and no others. This is what that costs.

case:     an identifier of neither shape
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_instance_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=sgp_instance_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN_sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN_«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xsgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      x«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567suffix
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567.
out:      the token is «sourcegraph-access-token».

# Tokens written together. No token can begin inside another here: everything a
# span covers past the prefix is a hexadecimal character, a separator or a
# letter of the word local, and the s the prefix opens with is none of those and
# neither of the two characters behind it in the prefix. So tokens written with
# nothing between them are separate values and all of them go, and a prefix
# standing where an identifier would have to hold it ends the candidate in front
# of it and opens the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a token of each form written together
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sgp_local_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567sgp_0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»«sourcegraph-access-token»«sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     a prefix written in front of a token
in:       sgp_sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp_«sourcegraph-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Forty hexadecimal characters
# behind the prefix are the vendor's format exactly, and a SHA-1 is forty of
# them, so the prefix written straight in front of one is a token character for
# character and the whole of it goes. A SHA-256 is longer and is redacted for
# forty-four characters with the rest left in the text. Sparing these would mean
# declining every token Sourcegraph ever issued, since there is nothing left in
# the text to tell the two apart.

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-1
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-256
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «sourcegraph-access-token»89abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix in front of a digest in a path
in:       assets/sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.png
out:      assets/«sourcegraph-access-token»89abcdef0123456789abcdef.png

case:     the prefix in front of an md5
in:       sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      sgp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       sgp_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      sgp_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

# The version of this token that carries no prefix. Sourcegraph documents it,
# still authenticates it, and it is forty hexadecimal characters with nothing in
# front of them — a git commit name, a SHA-1 of anything, the digest half of a
# lock file line. Reading it would take meaning out of text rather than a
# secret, so the prefix is required and these pass through whole.

case:     a bare value
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a commit written into a log line
in:       checked out 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      checked out 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a value assigned to the name the cli reads a token from
in:       SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SRC_ACCESS_TOKEN=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# And what else this pattern leaves alone: the prefix, which is read in the case
# Sourcegraph writes it and with every character of it, then a run of the right
# length with no prefix in front of it and the prefix the vendor's parser
# accepts but nothing the vendor runs writes.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       SGP_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      SGP_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the prefix without the underscore closing it
in:       sgp0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678
out:      sgp0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef012345678

case:     a hyphen where the prefix closes
in:       sgp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     the prefix with an h behind it
in:       sgph_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sgph_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And the text a token is written among, which this pattern has nothing to say
# about. The word Sourcegraph's own name, host names and paths are spelled with
# opens with the letters of the prefix and runs on past the underscore closing
# it, which is what turns each of them away.

case:     a log line naming the instance a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="fetching repository" host=sourcegraph.example.com repo_name=github.com/acme/website
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="fetching repository" host=sourcegraph.example.com repo_name=github.com/acme/website

case:     the command line a search is run from
in:       src search -json 'repo:acme/website mask'
out:      src search -json 'repo:acme/website mask'

case:     the endpoint a token authenticates against
in:       SRC_ENDPOINT=https://sourcegraph.example.com
out:      SRC_ENDPOINT=https://sourcegraph.example.com
